title: Example API gateway is returning 5xx responses

entry.query: fields @timestamp, @message, status, authorizerLatency, requestId | filter status >= 500 and level = '%LEVEL%' | sort @timestamp desc

trace.label: example-request-handler
trace.query: fields @timestamp, @message, level, service, traceId | filter @message like /{{key}}/ | sort @timestamp desc

trace.label: example-downstream-worker
trace.query: fields @timestamp, @message, level, service | filter @message like /{{key}}/ | sort @timestamp desc

cases.description: the downstream worker could not open a connection in time
cases.prose: The downstream worker timed out connecting to its dependency. This is the known transient failure recorded in the runbook; it clears on retry.
cases.resolution: No action while the retry succeeds. Escalate if the rate exceeds the runbook's threshold.
followUps: Confirm the downstream dependency's own health dashboard is green.

cases.description: the authorizer rejected an expired token
cases.prose: The request carried an expired token, so the authorizer rejected it. This is expected client behaviour, not a platform fault.
cases.resolution: No action. The caller refreshes its token and retries.

cases.description: the request handler dereferenced an absent payload field
cases.prose: The request handler failed on an absent payload field. This defect is open against the owning team.
cases.resolution: Track the open defect; no operator action resolves it.

cases.description: the request handler could not deserialise an upstream response
cases.prose: The request handler could not deserialise an upstream response. The recorded fix shipped, so a recurrence needs consensus before it is treated as known.
cases.resolution: The recorded fix is already released — reopen with the evidence below.

followUps: Check the gateway's 5xx metric graph for the same window.
Capture the verdict in the incident record.
